newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says will stick with easy monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: SNB says will stick with easy monetary policy.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) on Friday said it would stick with its easy monetary policy stance in 1997 and not raise interest rates until there are clear signs of growth in Switzerland's stagnant economy.
"The board of the Swiss National Bank, in agreement with the Swiss government, is continuing its easier monetary policy," the SNB said in a statement released before its semi-annual news conference.
"It intends to keep seasonally adjusted central bank money supply above the medium-term target path in 1997 as well."
The SNB's medium-term target for growth in the M0 central bank money supply aggregate is one percent per year.
"In doing so, it (the SNB) dully takes account of the unfavourable economic situation and the uncertainties surrounding European monetary integration," the statement said.
"The supply of money will remain abundant, creating the monetary preconditions for economic recovery," it added.
The SNB said its three-man policy-making board considered the current inflation risk in Switzerland to be slight.
"Nevertheless, it is aware that the time for a change of direction must be carefully chosen if price stability is to be maintained in the medium term," the SNB said.
"A change in monetary policy, however, will only enter into consideration once the Swiss economy is clearly on an uptrend," the statement said.
The SNB said it expected Swiss real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to grow by around 0.5 percent and the average inflation rate to amount to one percent in 1997.
It said these conditions meant demand for base money was likely to grow only slowly.
